metadata.notes: The worked example from CONCEPT.md §5 ('World Layer understands PEEL, requires: knife, creates: peeled potato, potato peel'). Byproducts are read from the target entity's producedByproducts, not hardcoded here — see ActionOutputsSchema. CORRECTED 2026-08-15: this note used to also cite CLAUDE_DEV_CTX.md's 'you cannot peel a potato that is already boiled' as a real constraint — that claim is factually wrong (boil-in-jacket-then-peel is a real, common technique, e.g. for potato salad), caught on direct user correction the same day ingredient.ts's invalidTransitions was built to enforce it. Never actually enforced against that specific claim; see potato.json's invalidTransitionsNote for what IS enforced instead.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: FALSE — a real, concrete finding, not a cautious default. PEEL neither destroysTarget nor has a statePrerequisite blocking re-running it on an already-peeled target: a blind retry after an interruption would spawn a SECOND potato_peel/egg_shell byproduct instance that doesn't physically exist — you cannot peel a potato twice and get two peels. A robot's fault-recovery layer must check current state before retrying PEEL specifically, not just re-issue the last step.

verification.description: Skin/shell/peel fully absent from the target's surface

hazards.note: Requires a knife — blade-to-hand contact risk
